subject: English
stem: The author's main purpose in this passage is to
optB: tell why vacations have become more common.
optC: contrast holidays and festive occasions with vacation.
optD: demonstrate that vacations are not really necessary.
solution: The passage centres on why modern man needs vacations now more than before (tension, monotonous work, renewal). Matches option B.
context: Vacations were once the prerogative of the privileged few, even as late as the nineteenth century. Now they are considered the right of all, except for such unfortunate masses as in China, for whom life, except for sleep and brief periods of rest, is uninterrupted toil. They are more necessary now than before because the average life is well rounded and has become increasingly departmentalised. The idea of vacations, as we conceive it must be incomprehensible to primitive people. Rest of some kind has of course always been a part of the rhythm of human life, but earlier ages did not find it necessary to organise it in the way that modern man has done. Holidays, feast days, were sufficient. With modern man's increasing tensions, with the useless quality of so much of his work, this break in the year's routine became steadily more necessary. Vacations became necessary for the purpose of renewal and repair.

(S1) The traveller said, "Can you tell me the way to the nearest inn?" ... (S6) "Thanks a lot."
P. "Do you want one in which you can spend the night?"

R. "Go right down the road and turn to the left."
S. "Yes", replied the traveller.
solution: Dialogue order: the traveller asks whether the peasant can help (S1); the peasant replies 'Yes' (Q); the peasant then asks whether he wants an inn to spend the night in (P); the traveller replies 'Yes' (S); the peasant gives the directions (R); the traveller thanks him (S6). stem: Which pair of compounds are chain isomers?
solution: Chain isomers differ in the branching of the carbon skeleton with the same molecular formula. n-Butane and isobutane are both C₄H₁₀ differing only in chain branching. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which pair of compounds are positional isomers?
solution: Positional isomers have the same skeleton and functional group but differ in its position. 1-Propanol and 2-propanol differ only in the position of the OH group. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry

solution: Position isomers have the same skeleton differing only in the position of a substituent/group. 1-Bromopropane and 2-bromopropane differ only in the position of Br on the same propane chain. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: How many positional isomers are possible for C₄H₈Br₂?
solution: Positional isomers keep the same n-butane skeleton and vary the positions of the two Br atoms: 1,1-; 1,2-; 1,3-; 1,4-; 2,2-; and 2,3-dibromobutane = 6 positional isomers. None of the options (2, 3, 4, 5) equals 6, so the item is flawed.

stem: Which pair shows functional isomerism?
solution: Functional isomers share a molecular formula but belong to different functional classes. Ethanol (alcohol) and dimethyl ether (ether) are both C₂H₆O, a classic functional-isomer pair. Matches option B.

stem: How many chain isomers are possible for C₅H₁₂?
solution: C₅H₁₂ has three isomers — n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane) and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane) — all chain isomers. So 3 chain isomers. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which compound is a ring-chain isomer of hex-1-ene?
solution: Hex-1-ene is C₆H₁₂; a ring-chain isomer must be a saturated ring with the same formula C₆H₁₂. Cyclohexane is C₆H₁₂. Cyclopentane is C₅H₁₀ and benzene is C₆H₆, so neither qualifies. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Option B Methylcyclopentane is also C₆H₁₂ and is technically a ring-chain isomer too; Cyclohexane is the standard/intended key.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Fullerene C60 has how many fused five-membered rings?
solution: Buckminsterfullerene C60 has a truncated-icosahedron structure made of 12 pentagons (five-membered rings) and 20 hexagons. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Fullerene C70 is made up of how many pentagons and hexagons?
solution: Fullerene C70 retains 12 pentagons (as required by Euler's rule for closed carbon cages) but has 25 hexagons, the extra ring belt giving its elongated shape. Matches option A.

stem: In angiosperms, pollen grain germinates to produce two male gametes. Which one of the following functions is carried out by these gametes?

optB: Both the gametes fuse with two different egg cells
